disagreements.topic: FY28 revenue base (and the round-1 supervisor's own figure)
disagreements.positions: Agent 1 uses FY28 ~$3.8-3.9B (+55%) and agent 2 ~$3.7-3.8B, both following the round-1 supervisor's '$3.8-3.9B implied by consensus EPS'. Agents 3 and 5 moved only part way, to $3.7B (+48%) and $3.65B (+46%). Agent 4 uses +50-55%.
disagreements.resolution: Consensus (StockAnalysis read 2026-10-26; now cited to 24/7 Wall St [src 55] and TIKR [src 54]) shows next-year (FY28) revenue $3.88B (+55% on FY27 $2.50B) and EPS $9.71, whose basis (GAAP or non-GAAP) neither source states, so no net margin is inferred from it and it enters no number; Zacks' FY28 EPS is $8.30 [src 28] on a basis below company non-GAAP. The $3.69B FY28 / $4.80B FY29 figures this round first used could not be verified and are dropped, and no public FY29 consensus was found. On $3.88B, the round-1 supervisor's $3.8-3.9B was right: agents 1 and 2 are on consensus and agents 3 and 5 ($3.7B, $3.65B) are ~5-6% below it. What matters at the horizon is NTM revenue at Sep-2027 (H2 FY28 + H1 FY29), which cannot be pinned to a public consensus. Net effect on the mean fair value is small.
disagreements.evidence: Consensus as read 2026-10-26 on StockAnalysis (FY27 $2.50B / EPS $6.31; FY28 $3.88B / EPS $9.71); the page as served on 2026-11-16 shows an older vintage, so the figures are now cited to 24/7 Wall St 2026-11-10 (FY27 $2.50B, EPS $6.3093; FY28 EPS $9.7121) [src 55] and TIKR (FY28 revenue $3.88B) [src 54]; neither states the EPS basis. 24/7 Wall St (FY28 EPS $8.69 -> $9.70 in 90 days, 14 up-revisions).

disagreements.topic: NTM EPS weighting at the horizon (agent 5)
disagreements.positions: Agent 5 builds Sep-2027 NTM EPS as 0.7 x FY28 + 0.3 x FY29 and states ~$9.90; on its own FY28 $8.90 and FY29 $11.80 that weighting gives $9.77 (0.7 x 8.90 + 0.3 x 11.80), and its $238 P/E leg is 24 x the stated $9.90. Agents 1, 2 and 4 use ~$10.0-10.4 and agent 3 uses $11.3.
disagreements.resolution: Credo's fiscal year ends around 1 May, so on 2027-09-25 Q1 FY28 has been reported and the NTM window is Q3-Q4 FY28 plus Q1-Q2 FY29, about 50/50 FY28/FY29. On agent 5's own FY28 $8.90 and FY29 $11.80, NTM EPS is ~$10.35 (0.5 x 8.90 + 0.5 x 11.80), not $9.77 (its 0.7/0.3 weighting) or the ~$9.90 it states. At its 24x, its P/E leg becomes ~$248 (from $238), which lifts its blend by ~$4-5. No consensus NTM EPS is computed: the FY28 consensus EPS sources found do not state their basis and no public FY29 consensus was found. Every agent except agent 3 haircuts consensus 7-10% in its base case and also carries a separate 25-33% bear scenario, which partly double-counts the same concentration and competition risk.
disagreements.evidence: Q1 FY27 reported 2026-09-01 for the quarter ended ~Aug 1; StockAnalysis FY28 EPS $9.71 (read 2026-10-26).

disagreements.positions: Agent 4 applies 9x NTM sales ($184). Agents 2, 3 and 5 use 11-11.5x and agent 1 uses 10x ($212-240).
disagreements.resolution: At management's FY27 non-GAAP net-margin outlook of ~50% [src 22], agent 4's own 22x P/E leg is equivalent to ~11x sales. A 9x sales multiple implies ~18x earnings, so the two legs contradict each other. At 11x on its own $4.0B NTM revenue plus $1.8B cash over 205M shares, the leg is ~$223, which lifts agent 4's blend from $216 to ~$226. The multiple regime is compressing (Mizuho cut its target to $245 from $290 on lower peer multiples), so I do not push anyone above 11.5x.
disagreements.evidence: Agent 4 method inputs; Investing.com on the Mizuho note; management's FY27 non-GAAP net-margin outlook 'in the vicinity of 50%' [src 22].

disagreements.resolution: Not settled by search, so I keep the mean (~21%). The concentration is real: end customers are 33% and 28% and one direct customer is 43% of revenue and 57% of receivables, and the three-month crash was driven by concentration fears, not by fundamentals. The funding backdrop cuts both ways. S&P sees six hyperscalers spending ~$1.3T in 2027, but only Microsoft is forecast to be free-cash-flow positive, so a 2027 digestion is a live risk. My searches did not confirm a documented Marvell share win at Amazon for 1.6T AECs.
disagreements.evidence: 24/7 Wall St crash analysis; Motley Fool on 2027 hyperscaler capex and FCF.

drivers.label: Copper scaling base: Big-4 capex x 0.60% (a scaling device, not a market size), calendar year paired with the fiscal year
drivers.source: Big-4 capex path: the project's shared path from the NVDA 2026-11-09 round [src 35] (CY2025 $410.0B; CY2026 $750.70B on the shared path's quarter basis: H1 CY2026 on its scaled cash basis $321.4B (XBRL cash PP&E x 1.0903) + Q3 $207.41B as reported + Q4 $221.88B (each company's 2026 guide less its 9-month spend) [src 35]; the Q3 calls' 2026 guides themselves sum to $730.1B on the companies' own basis (Microsoft ~$170B, Alphabet $195-205B, Amazon ~$220B, Meta $135-145B [src 36, 37, 38, 39]), and the NVDA set states both figures; CY2027 $1,013.88B and CY2028 $1,359.36B per company from the business its capacity serves), replacing the 10-23 project build (733/1,080/1,330 [src 23]), x a copper attach of 0.60% of capex (estimate). No citable copper TAM: Credo's FY2026 10-K has no market-opportunity figure [src 12]; management calls ALC, scale-up and OmniConnect 'multibillion dollar' opportunities without a copper figure [src 22].
drivers.derivation: PLAIN READING (Kilian 2026-11-16 16:15Z): copper revenue grows with Big-4 capex; this is not a market share. The 0.60% attach is a scaling device with no source: share is calibrated to Credo's actual copper revenue, so the attach level cancels and copper revenue = Q1 FY27 copper x capex growth x (1 - MaxLinear loss). No current public AEC market forecast was found: LightCounting's December 2023 newsletter put AOC, DAC and AEC sales at $2.8B by 2028 (stale, src 97); its December 2025 update is a paid report ($5,995, no figures on the public page, src 98), and 650 Group's AEC report publishes no figure in its launch release (src 99). Update 2026-11-13 (tape-hold read-through, 2026-11-16): capex path moved to the shared NVDA 11-09 hs_capex so every AI-capex name reads one path. TAM = Big-4 capex x 0.60%: CY2025 410 x 0.006 = $2.46B; CY2026 750.70 x 0.006 = $4.504B; CY2027 1,013.88 x 0.006 = $6.083B; CY2028 1,359.36 x 0.006 = $8.156B (was 4.398 / 6.48 / 7.98). The 0.60% attach is a calibration: it makes Credo's FY2026 copper revenue (~$1,275M, see segment base) ~52% of the TAM; MaxLinear's CEO estimated that Credo accounts for 93% to 99% of the AEC cable market (Stocktwits' paraphrase of the call [src 40]), and Marvell retimers are the most widely adopted by AEC integrators [src 43], so Credo's share of the wider copper wallet (AECs plus retimers/PHYs) is below its AEC share. Cross-check: LightCounting puts optics sales to the top five cloud providers at 2.7% of their capex in 2025 (Lightwave 2026-03-10 on the 'Optics for AI Clusters' report [src 33]), so copper at 0.6% is ~1/5 of the optics spend (0.6 / 2.7 = 0.22). The attach level cancels in revenue (copper_share is calibrated to it); what moves value is the capex growth and the share trend. Fiscal/calendar alignment: Credo's FY n runs May n-1 to April n (FY2026 ended 2026-05-02), so 8 of its 12 months fall in CY n-1; FY n is paired with CY n-1 (FY26 = CY2025, FY27 = CY2026, FY28 = CY2027, FY29 = CY2028), (calendar arithmetic; the pairing is the nearest calendar year, not a stated lead). drivers.label: Copper revenue / copper scaling base (calibrated to Credo's copper revenue; not a market share)
drivers.source: Base: FY2026 copper revenue ~$1,275.1M (estimate, segment base row) / CY2025 copper TAM $2.46B = 51.8%. Forecast quarters (gate fix 2026-11-16, bottom-up): copper revenue grows from the Q1 FY27 level with the shared Big-4 capex path [src 35] (Q1-Q2 CY2029, beyond the path: Dell'Oro's July 2026 forecast has worldwide data-center capex above $3 trillion by 2030 with the Top 4 US hyperscalers about half [src 67], which on the shared CY2028 gives +5.0% a year for CY2029-30; estimate), less a MaxLinear 1.6T AEC share loss: MaxLinear targets 20-30% of the 1.6T AEC market 'over the next couple of years', selling silicon to cable makers, initial focus 'one or two large U.S. data centers' [src 40]; initial 1.6T revenue in 2027, stronger volumes in 2028 [src 41]; 1.6T ~56% of 2027 pluggable optical transceiver revenue (TrendForce [src 42]; used as the proxy for the 1.6T share of AEC revenue in Q1 FY28; held at 56% for FY28-29: HSBC has 3.2T at ~30% of high-speed transceiver units by 2028 [src 66, a relay of a non-public note], so the 1.6T-only share need not keep rising; no source gives a 2028-29 1.6T revenue share); AEC share of copper revenue 0.90 (estimate, bounded below at ~88% by the FY26 10-K's 'contributed over 99% of the increase in revenue' [src 12; phrase located by EDGAR full-text search, src 51] and the FY25 10-K revenue split and its 'AEC products, which contributed over 95% of the increase in product sales' [src 30; phrase located by EDGAR full-text search, src 60], arithmetic in the derivation). Credo sells to 'hyperscalers, Neoclouds, OEMs, ODMs, CMs and optical module manufacturers' [src 12].
drivers.derivation: PLAIN READING (Kilian 2026-11-16 16:15Z): copper revenue grows with Big-4 capex; this is not a market share. The 0.60% attach is a scaling device with no source: share is calibrated to Credo's actual copper revenue, so the attach level cancels and copper revenue = Q1 FY27 copper x capex growth x (1 - MaxLinear loss). No current public AEC market forecast was found: LightCounting's December 2023 newsletter put AOC, DAC and AEC sales at $2.8B by 2028 (stale, src 97); its December 2025 update is a paid report ($5,995, no figures on the public page, src 98), and 650 Group's AEC report publishes no figure in its launch release (src 99). Gate fix 2026-11-16 (replaces the FY27 share taken from the >85% growth guide and consensus, and the H2 quarters shaped to them): copper_q = Q1 FY27 copper 444 (fifth gate fix: 479.0 less optical 35.0 within the 10-Q's 'over 90%' AEC cap [src 11]; was 424 on optical 55) x (Big-4 capex in the paired calendar quarter / capex in Q3 CY2026) x (1 - MaxLinear loss_q). Pairing (estimate, confidence low): each Credo quarter is paired with the calendar quarter after the one it overlaps most (Q1 FY27 May-Jul 2026 with Q3 CY2026, ... Q2 FY29 with Q4 CY2028, Q4 FY29 with Q2 CY2029), because part of Credo's revenue is billed to ODMs, CMs and module makers [src 12] before the finished racks reach the hyperscalers' capex. The lead is our estimate (confidence low): no source states it or sizes it; the no-lead (same-quarter) pairing is sized in judgment_alternatives (+5.59% (engine, 2026-11-17 booked set, research target (12m) 211.94)) and carded. Shared path quarters [src 35]: Q3 CY2026 207.41, Q4 221.88, CY2027 233.85 / 246.47 / 259.77 / 273.79, CY2028 297.98 / 324.30 / 352.95 / 384.13 ($B). Q1-Q2 CY2029 (fourth gate fix; replaces +12% carried from Goldman Sachs' 2028 rate, which no 2029 source supported): the shared path ends at CY2028; Dell'Oro's July 2026 forecast puts worldwide data-center capex above $3 trillion by 2030 with the Top 4 US hyperscalers about half [src 67], so ~$1,500B for the Top 4 in 2030; on the shared CY2028 $1,359.36B that is (1,500 / 1,359.36)^(1/2) - 1 = +5.0% a year, CY2029 $1,428.0B (estimate, confidence low: Dell'Oro's series is data-center capex, the shared path is total capex), spread at a constant quarterly rate from Q4 CY2028 (-2.91% a quarter: 372.95 / 362.10; a +5% year lands below four quarters at the Q4 CY2028 exit because CY2028 ramps through the year); Goldman Sachs' +12% carried (-0.02%), flat at Q4 CY2028 (-0.02%) and +17% (-0.03%) alternatives sized (engine, 2026-11-17 booked set, research target (12m) 211.94). Copper before dc_mor: Q2 FY27 475.0, Q3 500.6, Q4 527.6 (FY27 $1,947.2M); FY28 544.4 / 561.5 / 597.7 / 635.9 ($2,339.5M); FY29 676.2 / 718.7 / 697.8 / 677.5 ($2,770.2M). share_q = copper_q x 4 / (year TAM x 1000). MaxLinear loss_q = AEC share of copper 0.90 x 1.6T share of AEC revenue (56% from TrendForce's 2027 pluggable optical mix [src 42], used as a proxy for AECs, held through FY29 (fourth gate fix; was +2pt a quarter to 70%, which no source supported): HSBC has 3.2T at ~30% of high-speed transceiver units by 2028 [src 66, a relay of a non-public note], so 1.6T alone need not keep rising after 2027; no source gives a 2028-29 1.6T revenue share; the old rise to 70%, which reads MaxLinear as contesting 3.2T AECs too, is sized at -1.19%) x MaxLinear share of 1.6T AEC (linear ramp from Q1 FY28, first revenue 2027 [src 41], to the 25% midpoint of its 20-30% target by Q2 FY29, two years after the call (Quartr dates it 23 Oct 2026 [src 41]; Stocktwits write-up 2026-10-23 [src 40]), then held): FY28 2.1% / 4.2% / 6.3% / 8.4%, FY29 10.5% / 12.6% / 12.6% / 12.6%. AEC share of copper 0.90 (estimate, confidence medium): the FY26 10-K says the AEC ramp 'contributed over 99% of the increase in revenue' [src 12, 51], so FY26 non-AEC revenue rose by less than 1% x 898.3 = $9.0M. FY25 non-AEC revenue is at most IP licensing $12.5M + engineering services $12.1M + non-AEC product sales [src 30] (both amounts checked 2026-11-17 by EDGAR full-text search, 10-K forms, CIK 1807794: 'engineering services' with '12.1 million' and 'IP license' with '12.5' hit only the FY25 10-K, acc 0001628280-25-033813, crdo-20250503.htm, and the FY24 10-K, acc 0001628280-24-029629); the FY25 10-K says 'AEC products, which contributed over 95% of the increase in product sales' (phrase confirmed by EDGAR full-text search: among 10-Ks the only hit is the FY25 10-K; four 10-Qs also carry it [src 60]), so even if every FY24 product dollar was non-AEC (FY24 revenue $193.0M less 15% IP = $164.1M) non-AEC product sales were at most 164.1 + 5% x (412.2 - 164.1) = $176.5M, FY25 non-AEC at most $201.1M and FY26 at most $210.1M; less optical ~$60M leaves at most $150.1M of non-AEC copper, so AECs are at least 1,125.0 / 1,275.1 = 88.2% of FY26 copper (worst case; arithmetic, not a stated share). 0.90 sits just above that bound (moderately conservative: a higher AEC share means a larger MaxLinear loss). Why book the loss (base case moderately conservative, Kilian 2026-11-10): a named competitor gave a share target on its call and dates its revenue; Marvell's retimer chips are 'the most widely adopted by AEC system integrators (more than Broadcom's)' [src 43]. Against: MaxLinear sells silicon, not cables, the target is its own, it focuses on one or two large US data centers, and its CEO estimated Credo at 93% to 99% of the AEC cable market (Stocktwits paraphrase [src 40]); management says 'AECs remain our largest business and continues to grow', it has 'deep relationships with 5 hyperscalers', sees 'increased AEC penetration' within existing customers, and its fourth 10% customer in Q1 FY27 was a returning former 10% customer [src 22]; it also expects 'additional customer ramps during fiscal 27 across both 800-gig and 1.6T' [src 22], which this build does not size (upside). Cross-checks only (not inputs): Q2 FY27 total 531.6 vs the $525-535M guide [src 10] (+0.3% on the midpoint); FY27 total $2,372.7M (+77.7%) vs the '>85%' guide [src 22] and the Zacks $2.50B consensus [src 28]. Actual quarters: copper = reported revenue (8-K Ex-99.1 releases (acc 0001807794-25-000018, 0001628280-25-054428, 0001628280-26-013205, 0001628280-26-039474): 223.1 / 268.0 / 407.0 / 437.0; Q1 FY27 8-K Ex-99.1 acc 0001628280-26-059795 / 10-Q acc 0001628280-26-060111: 479.0) less estimated optical (10 / 12 / 17 / 21; Q1 FY27 35.0, capped by the 10-Q's 'over 90%' AEC share of the y/y rise [src 11]). Seasonality: none usable; FY25 quarter shares 13.7/16.5/30.9/38.9% (Q1 FY25 59.8 = FY25 436.8 [F2] - 72.0 - 135.0 - 170.0) and FY26 16.7/20.1/30.5/32.7% are the ramp, not a calendar pattern. ALC is placed in optical, OmniConnect gearboxes (electrical, first revenue FY28 [src 22]) here. Bear: dual-sourcing at the top customer is carried by top_customer_pct, not here.

drivers.label: Non-GAAP gross margin, copper (AECs, electrical ICs, SerDes IP)
drivers.source: Not disclosed by line. Base solved from the FY2026 blended non-GAAP gross margin 68.14% ($909.8M / $1,335.1M, Q4 FY26 release reconciliation [src 13]) with optical at 65% and 4.49% of revenue. Reported blended non-GAAP GM 67.6% / 67.7% / 68.6% / 68.3% (FY26 quarters [src 16, 15, 14, 13]) and 68.0% (Q1 FY27 [src 10]); FY27 blended guide 'broadly consistent with fiscal year 26 levels' and Q2 67-69% [src 22, 10]. FY28-29 price pressure: Marvell's retimers 'typically priced 15-20% below Credo's when supplied to third-party buyers' (Semi Fundamental [src 43]; the author attributes it to secondhand channel feedback, 'we heard', not a measured price); MaxLinear sells AEC silicon to cable makers, initial focus 'one or two large U.S. data centers' [src 40]; 1.6T ~56% of 2027 pluggable optical transceiver revenue [src 42] (proxy for the AEC mix, held through FY29); 3.2T ~30% of high-speed transceiver units by 2028 (HSBC via Exencial, relay [src 66]); top two end customers 33% + 28% [src 11].
drivers.derivation: Base (0.6814 - 0.04494 x 0.65) / 0.95506 = 68.29%. Actual quarters solved from the reported blended non-GAAP GM with optical at 65% (Q1 FY27 68.0% on optical 35.0 and copper 444.0 -> copper (0.680 x 479.0 - 0.65 x 35.0) / 444.0 = 68.24%; fifth gate fix, was 68.39% on the 55 / 424 split). FY27 (Q2-Q4): held at the Q1 FY27 68.24%: the blended margin stayed in 67.6-68.6% across the last five reported quarters while revenue rose from $223.1M to $479.0M [src 16, 15, 14, 13, 10], the Q2 guide is 67-69% [src 10], and no competing 1.6T AEC silicon ships before MaxLinear's first revenue in 2027 [src 41]. FY28-29 (second gate fix 2026-11-16, replaces the Q1 level held flat): the real-world case is price pressure on 1.6T AECs once cables built on competing retimer silicon ship. Marvell's retimer chips sell 15-20% below Credo's to third parties per Semi Fundamental's secondhand channel feedback ('we heard' [src 43]; not a measured price) and MaxLinear's silicon goes to cable makers for one or two large US data centers [src 40]; the gap is on the chip, which is only part of a cable's cost, so the cable-level gap is smaller: Credo is assumed to cut 1.6T AEC prices by 7.5% (half the 15% low end of the chip gap; estimate, confidence low) where a second source exists. Contested share of copper revenue c_q = AEC share 0.90 x 1.6T share of AEC revenue (56% = TrendForce's 2027 1.6T share of pluggable optical transceiver revenue [src 42], used as a proxy for AECs, held through FY29 (fourth gate fix; was +2pt a quarter to 70%, which no source supported): HSBC has 3.2T at ~30% of high-speed transceiver units by 2028 [src 66, relay], see copper_share) x 0.61 (MaxLinear's one or two US data centers, taken as Credo's top two end customers, 33% + 28% [src 11, 40]). With costs unchanged, GM_q = (0.682365 - 0.075 c_q) / (1 - 0.075 c_q): 67.49% in every FY28-29 quarter (-0.75pt). Direction: the evidence points down (new competitors, chip-price gap) and none points up for FY28-29. Alternatives sized (all under 5%): no price response (68.24%) +0.79%; full 17.5% chip gap matched on the contested volume -1.12%; the 7.5% cut on all 1.6T volume -0.53%; the old mix rise to 70% (67.49% to 67.30%) -0.11% (engine, 2026-11-17 booked set, research target (12m) 211.94). IP licensing carries almost no cost: FY25 IP license cost of revenue $171K on IP license revenue $12,476K = 1.37% (FY24 $816K on $28,024K) (FY25 10-K statement of operations, R5 [src 30]), so its small share of copper revenue lifts the copper margin slightly; it is inside the solved base, not a separate input. Blended GM from the segments after dc_mor (engine, 2026-11-17 booked set): FY27 66.6%, FY28 63.3%, FY29 63.3%, with optics on the booked Coherent anchor (Kilian card 2026-11-16 17:36Z; revenue-weighted optical GM 59.2% / 56.8% / 57.1%) at 18% / 39% / 40% of revenue (replaces the blend on the superseded 65% optical margin).

drivers.label: AI-cluster Ethernet optical transceivers (100G+) and CPO, scale-out and scale-up (LightCounting definition), calendar year paired with the fiscal year
drivers.source: CY2025 $16.5B: LightCounting's January 2026 forecast for AI-cluster Ethernet optics as quoted in POET Technologies' FY2025 Form 20-F ('$26 billion in 2026, up ~60% year-over-year from $16.5 billion in 2025') [src 31]; LightCounting's own page returns HTTP 403. Lightwave's 2026-03-10 write-up of the same report prints $8B for 2025 [src 33]; the base level cancels in revenue (optical_share is calibrated to it on FY27 revenue), so only the growth path moves value. Growth: LightCounting's October forecast for Ethernet optical transceivers, +120% for 2026 and +76% for 2027, declining to +20% by 2031 (Lightwave 2026-10-08 [src 32]), applied to the AI-cluster market; its January AI-cluster Ethernet optics figure was +60% for 2026 [src 31]: two different LightCounting series, not one forecast revised.
drivers.derivation: CY2026 16.5 x 2.20 = $36.3B; CY2027 36.3 x 1.76 = $63.888B; CY2028: LightCounting's optics-to-capex ratio (Kilian 2026-10-27 17:21Z, replacing the straight-line interpolation of growth rates): optics sales to the top five cloud providers were 2.7% of their capex in 2025 and 3.1% in 2026, rising to 4.1% by 2031 (Lightwave 2026-03-10 on LightCounting's 'Optics for AI Clusters' [src 33]); linear between 2026 and 2031 (+0.2pt a year) gives 3.3% in 2027 and 3.5% in 2028. CY2028 growth = (Big-4 capex 1,359.36 / 1,013.88, the shared path [src 35]) x (3.5% / 3.3%) = 1.3408 x 1.0606 = 1.4220; 63.888 x 1.4220 = $90.85B (update 2026-11-13; was 1,330/1,080 x 1.0606 = 1.306, $83.438B). Cross-check: the pluggable transceiver market grows from 60 million units in 2026 to 175 million by 2030 (CEO quoting market forecasters, Q1 FY27 call [src 22]), (175/60)^(1/4) - 1 = +30.7% a year in units. CY2026-27 keep LightCounting's published growth rates (+120%, +76%) because they are published figures; the same ratio method would give +57% for 2027 (1,080/733 x 3.3/3.1), so the 2027 step is the richer of the two. Fiscal/calendar alignment: Credo's FY n runs May n-1 to April n (FY2026 ended 2026-05-02), so 8 of its 12 months fall in CY n-1; FY n is paired with CY n-1 (FY26 = CY2025, FY27 = CY2026, FY28 = CY2027, FY29 = CY2028), (calendar arithmetic; the pairing is the nearest calendar year, not a stated lead). Variants (engine-sized on the 2026-11-17 booked set, research target (12m) 211.94, judgment_alternatives): CY2028 tied to Big-4 capex growth alone (1,359.36 / 1,013.88 = +34.1%, $85.66B) -1.35%; the straight-line interpolation of LightCounting growth rates (+62%, $103.5B) +3.30%; the pre-update ratio build ($83.438B) -1.93%; LightCounting's ~+20% a year long-run rate from the same report ($8B 2025 -> $20B 2030 [src 33]) applied to CY2027-28 ($43.6B / $52.4B) -17.12% (carded); the CEO-quoted pluggable-transceiver unit growth, 60M units 2026 -> 175M 2030 = +30.7% a year [src 22], applied to CY2027-28 ($47.44B / $62.01B; units, not dollars, so any change in price per unit is left out) -13.26% (carded). The two 2026 growth figures are different LightCounting series: +60% for AI-cluster Ethernet optics in the January vintage quoted by POET [src 31], +120% for Ethernet optical transceivers in the October forecast [src 32]; the set applies the newer transceiver rate to the AI-cluster market (estimate). Vintage gap: our CY2026 $36.3B (16.5 x 2.20, October vintage) is above the $26B for 2026 in LightCounting's January vintage as quoted by POET [src 31] (36.3 / 26 - 1 = +40%); the October +120% (transceiver series) is the newer figure, so it is used; on the January AI-cluster series FY27 optical revenue would not change (optical FY27 is built by product line, not from the TAM), only the base share. QUARTERS (2026-10-29): Each quarter carries its fiscal year's calendar-year LightCounting level; the within-year shape sits in optical_share. Actual quarters carry the same estimate.

drivers.source: Fifth gate fix 2026-11-16: Q1 FY27 optical capped by the 10-Q (AEC products 'contributed over 90% of the increase in revenue' [src 11]). Base: FY2026 optical revenue ~$60M (estimate, segment base row: optical DSPs only, 10 / 12 / 17 / 21 a quarter) / $16.5B = 0.364%. FY27 built by product line (fourth gate fix 2026-11-16): Q1 FY27 brought 'record revenue' in optical DSPs and the 'first silicon photonics PIC revenue following the Dust Photonics acquisition'; the initial PIC wins are in 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers, 'and we expect these products to ramp throughout the year'; ZF optics 'production shipments are underway' with 'additional customer ramps during fiscal 27 across both 800-gig and 1.6T'; '1.6T DSP revenue remains on track for later this fiscal year' (Q1 FY27 call [src 22]). ZF optics will be 'clearly our largest revenue contributor for our optical portfolio' with 'a very aggressive ramp in the second half' and 'even more than double or triple that the following year'; each of the three lines 'is going to grow more than 80% year over year' (Q4 FY26 call [src 61]). DustPhotonics: acquired 2026-05-28; no revenue since acquisition is disclosed and pro forma results were not presented because the effect was not material (Q1 FY27 10-Q [src 11]); its PICs are 'deployed in transceivers at leading hyperscale AI clusters' and it is fabless (April 2026 8-K [src 69]); all its wafers are fabricated at Tower Semiconductor [src 63]. Tower's silicon-photonics revenue: annualized Q2 2026 run rate above $680 million [src 68]; ~$240M in Q3 2026, a Q4 2026 run rate above $1.1 billion, and start capacity at 3x the Q3 2026 level by Q3 2027 (~$720M a quarter) [src 62]. DustPhotonics deal call (Quartr summary [src 53]): combined optical 'over $500 million' in FY2027, up to 3.21M contingent shares on financial milestones, no DustPhotonics revenue figure. Market: LightCounting +120% for 2026 Ethernet transceivers, +76% for 2027 [src 32]. Credo's ramp record: FY25 quarterly revenue 59.8 / 72.0 / 135.0 / 170.0 during the AEC ramp (FY25 10-K and releases [src 30, 20, 19, 18]). Company plan (guidance_check only): 'more than $600 million of optical revenue in fiscal 27', each line 'more than $100 million' [src 22, 61]. FY28: dated additions (two next-generation design-win ramps, ALC initial revenue, NPO design wins) [src 22]. drivers.label: Largest end customer's share of revenue (end-customer basis), as a concentration term
drivers.source: FY2026 10-K end-customer table: Customer D 33%, Customer B 32%, Customer E 19% (direct-billing basis Customer A 49%) [src 12]. Q1 FY27 10-Q end-customer table: D 33%, C 28%, E 13%, F 10% (direct basis A 43%, 57% of receivables) [src 11]; CFO: 'our largest customer was a third of our revenue at 33%' [src 22].
drivers.derivation: Base 0.33 (FY26) and held at 0.33 in FY27-29 (Q1 FY27 33%; management expects 3-4 customers above 10% [src 22], i.e. diversification comes through the other customers, which the shares carry). Formula: each segment's revenue = TAM x share x 1000 x (1 - 0.33) / (1 - top_customer_pct). At the base path the factor is 1. Moving the driver to T means the top customer buys less (or more) while every other customer stays as the TAM x share build says: total revenue scales by 0.67 / (1 - T) and the top customer's revenue by T x 0.67 / (0.33 x (1 - T)). Bear: T 0.33 -> 0.21 cuts total revenue 15.2% and the top customer's revenue 46% (a 1.6T AEC dual-source to Marvell at 15-20% lower prices, agents 1-5). The top customer's product mix is not disclosed; the term applies to copper and optical alike (the CFO says these hyperscalers buy more than AECs [src 22]). Variant view: on the direct-billing basis (43%) the same customer-loss story is larger; the end-customer basis is used because the sourcing decision is the end customer's. QUARTERS (2026-10-29): 0.33 every quarter: FY26 10-K end-customer D 33% (the FY figure is used for each FY26 quarter: an annual concentration figure applied to each base quarter, so the base quarters aggregate to the 10-K's 0.33; the 10-Q end-customer tables give the quarter's largest end customer at 35% Q1 (acc 0001807794-25-000021), 42% Q2 (0001628280-25-054549), 39% Q3 (0001628280-26-014017), Q4 not disclosed, with the letters rotating between filings, so the quarter tops are not the FY top); Q1 FY27 10-Q D 33% [src 11]; held forward. The term is 1 at 0.33, so it moves revenue only in scenarios.
drivers.why: Concentration: one hyperscaler is a third of revenue; the agents' main bear story is its sourcing decision.

drivers.source: Q1 FY27 10-Q / call: four end customers at or above 10%, 33% / 28% / 13% / 10% (84%), the top three 'similar to or the same 3 as in the prior quarter' [src 11, 22]; Q4 FY26: top end customers 34% / 27% / 16% (77% for the top three) and a new fourth 10% customer (Q4 FY26 call [src 61]; Zacks: four hyperscalers each >= 10% [src 48]); Q1 FY27 top three 33% / 28% / 13% (74%) on the 10-Q's end-customer table (Customer D 33%, C 28%, E 13%, F 10% [src 11]; CFO on the call: 'a third of our revenue at 33%, second largest 28, and then followed by 13 and 10' [src 22]); the 10-Q's direct-billing table (Customer A 43%, B 28% [src 11]) counts direct buyers (some end customers have their contract manufacturing partners place orders, src 11) and is not the basis (fifth gate fix: basis checked, value unchanged); 'We continue to expect that 3 to 4 customers will be greater than 10% of revenue in the coming quarters and fiscal year' and 'we continue to make progress in diversifying our revenue base across hyperscalers, neo clouds and other customers'; 'our engagement with Neo Cloud customers continues to expand' [src 22]; Credo has 'deep relationships with 5 hyperscalers' and growing neocloud and module customers [src 22]. Identity (not disclosed): Microsoft named by Credo as its first AEC customer [src 22]; Amazon ~86% of Q3 FY25 revenue per Needham [src 50]; the top three read as Microsoft, Amazon, Google, the fourth as Meta or xAI (opinion [src 49]). Self-funding hyperscalers = Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet and Meta, as Kilian defined the carve-out (2026-11-16); no outside financing note is cited for it.
drivers.derivation: Q1 FY27 0.74 = the top three end customers (33 + 28 + 13), counted as self-funding Big-4 hyperscalers; the fourth 10% customer (10%) is left exposed because it may be xAI (externally financed), and the remaining 16% (neoclouds, module makers, other) is exposed. Base case moderately conservative (Kilian 2026-11-10): only the three customers most likely to be Big-4 are carved out; the carve-out itself is Kilian's decision (2026-11-16). Path (fourth gate fix 2026-11-16; FY28-29 had extended a one-quarter slope): asked whether Tier 2 cloud customers could be 10 or 20% of revenue over the next few years, the CEO said neoclouds 'collectively' 'could be on the order of 20%' and will be a 'growing and more meaningful opportunity for Credo over the coming years' (Q4 FY26 call [src 61]); management is diversifying across 'hyperscalers, neo clouds and other customers' with 3 to 4 customers above 10% [src 22]. Neocloud revenue is not disclosed: it is taken at ~9% of revenue today (estimate, confidence low: part of the 16% outside the four 10% customers, which also holds OEMs, ODMs and module makers [src 12]), reaching 20% by Q4 FY29 (about three years after the June 2026 call) with the gain coming out of the top three: 11pt over 11 quarters, 1pt a quarter from Q2 FY27 (the top three's share fell 3pt, 77% -> 74%, from Q4 FY26 to Q1 FY27 [src 61, 11]): 0.73 / 0.72 / 0.71 in FY27, 0.70-0.67 in FY28, 0.66-0.63 in FY29 (year means 0.725 / 0.685 / 0.645). At 63% the top three would still be compatible with 3 to 4 customers above 10% (e.g. 28 / 21 / 14% plus a 10% fourth). Alternatives sized: 0.74 held flat +0.81%; all four 10% customers (84%) +1.99%; only the two named in reports (61%) -0.72%; neoclouds from a 4% base (top three to 0.58) -0.37%; from a 12% base (to 0.66) +0.22%; no carve-out -7.91% (Kilian decided the carve-out). Sizes: engine, 2026-11-17 booked set, research target (12m) 211.94. Customer names are not disclosed.
drivers.why: Kilian 2026-11-16: revenue from self-funding hyperscalers is left untouched by the moratorium haircut (they redirect builds); dc_mor applies to the rest.

Tech FCF-leg rule (Kilian 2026-11-17, src 86): peers' median plain FCF / market cap. Gate fix 2026-11-17 (basis-clean NTM step, replacing the consensus EPS-growth step, which mixed trailing GAAP EPS with Alpha Vantage forward EPS of unstated basis): each peer's NTM FCF = TTM plain FCF (operating cash flow less capex, SEC XBRL, src 85) x consensus NTM revenue / TTM revenue (SEC XBRL), i.e. the TTM FCF margin held; NTM revenue = consensus fiscal years time-weighted from 2026-11-16 (current FY share of the next 12 months, rest next FY); market cap at the 2026-11-16 close (src 85). ALAB: FCF $344.7M on TTM revenue $1,556.2M (22.1%); NTM 0.123 x $2.03B + 0.877 x $3.35B = $3.187B (src 87); x2.048 = 2.00% (trailing 0.97%). RMBS: $312.9M / $796.1M (39.3%); 0.123 x $828.3M + 0.877 x $997.6M = $976.7M (src 93, page last updated 2026-08-31); x1.227 = 4.60% (3.75%). COHR (-$1,833.6M), AAOI (-$315.2M) and FN (-$190.5M) have negative TTM FCF and ANET has no FCF tag in the pull: left out (a negative yield prices nothing); for AVGO, MTSI and CIEN the last few weeks of the window fall in a fiscal year the pages do not show, so their NTM revenue is slightly low. bear.story: Agents 1-5 bear (probabilities 0.25-0.33, median 0.25; values $100-120, median $110): the top end customer (33%; likely Amazon Trainium, the 43% direct customer) dual-sources 1.6T AECs to Marvell at 15-20% lower prices and/or hyperscalers digest 2027 capex; the H2 FY27 ramp slips. Restated as drivers: top_customer_pct 0.33 -> 0.21 (add -0.12: that customer's revenue -46%, total -15.2%, the rest unchanged), copper_tam and optical_tam -10% (capex digestion), gm_copper and gm_optical -3pt (agent_2: 62-64%); P/E -8 turns to 15.5x (agents 14-18x).

base.story: Copper = Q1 FY27 copper (444, inside the 10-Q's AEC cap) grown with the shared Big-4 capex quarters (one-quarter lead, estimate; CY2029 at +5.0% from Dell'Oro's 2030 end point) less a MaxLinear 1.6T loss (1.6T mix held at 56%), copper GM easing 0.75pt in FY28-29 on 1.6T price pressure; optical FY27 built by line (DSPs, PICs at Tower's SiPh output ramp, ZF optics as units x ASP from the capped Q1 to 200k a month by April 2027 at $400) at $426M, FY28 ZF units doubling at -25% a year ASP, DSPs and PICs with LightCounting's market; top customer held at 33%. Revenue $2,373M / $3,703M / $4,592M (optical $426M / $1,449M / $1,845M after dc_mor); blended GM 67.7% / 66.5% / 66.5%; opex = revenue x intensity (TTM 19.6% to Marvell's 21.55%): $473M / $792M / $985M; 15% minimum tax from FY28; 23.5x NTM EPS / 11x NTM sales before the x0.9944 growth term.

bull.story: Agents 1-5 bull (probabilities 0.22-0.25; values $345-380): Amazon Trn3 ramps strongly, Microsoft/Meta/Oracle and neoclouds broaden the base (3-4 customers >10%), optics pass a $1B run-rate, ALC/OmniConnect start; hyperscaler 2027 capex ~$1.2-1.3T. Restated: optical_share +15% (FY28 optical ~$1.4B), copper_share +5% (Credo holds 1.6T share), top_customer_pct +0.02 (Trn3: that customer +10%, total +3.1%), copper_tam and optical_tam +10%, gm +0.5pt both; P/E +3.5 turns to 27x.

guidance_check.drivers_note: Line build (optical_share): optical DSPs $140.9M (FY26 base at LightCounting's +120%), SiPh PICs $46.4M (first Q1 revenue at the ramp of Tower Semiconductor's silicon-photonics output), ZF optics $238.2M (units x ASP: 11.0k / 37.1k / 125.2k / 422.3k modules at $400, from the 10-Q-capped Q1 at a constant monthly rate to 200k a month in April 2027, the smallest reading of 'hundreds of thousands of units per month', which Benzinga reports as Credo's plan for ZF transceivers) = $425.5M; quarters 35.0 / 56.6 / 100.1 / 233.8.
guidance_check.why: Built by product line, not set at the floor (the >$600M is a cross-check only): $425.5M is 29.1% below the company's 'more than $600 million' [src 22]. Fifth gate fix: the 10-Q caps Q1 FY27 optical at ~35.6 (AEC products 'over 90% of the increase in revenue' [src 11]; the phrase is confirmed in that 10-Q by SEC full-text search [src 94]), so Q1 is 35.0 (was 55) and the ZF ramp starts from 4.4 (11.0k modules), which takes $126M out of FY27 ZF while the FY27 exit rate, and so FY28-29, are unchanged. ZF optics are complete transceivers at 'three digit' ASPs against two-digit DSPs and PICs [src 61]; the CEO gave a year-end rate of 'hundreds of thousands of units per month' without naming the product [src 70], which Benzinga reported in June as Credo's plan for 'ZF transceiver units' [src 76]; more than four ZF customers ramp in FY27 [src 71]. Why it lands below the floor: the Q1 start is capped, the exit rate is read at its smallest (200k a month), the module price at the 800G market $400 with no ZeroFlap premium or 1.6T mix [src 74], and the PIC line ($46.4M) at its foundry's output ramp because DustPhotonics brings little revenue of its own (pro forma results not material [src 11]). Against it: management has said '>$600M' twice, raised from 'greater than $500 million' in April [src 69, 22, 61], and beat all 8 first quarterly revenue guides (median +10.4%). The floor read for FY27 is +0.71%; the readings that move the target are FY28-29 (engine, 2026-11-17 set): ZF from its own '>$100M' line -31.16% (2x) / -27.58% (3x), the AEC-ramp shape -34.71%, ZF FY28 at 2x revenue -23.81%, exit 300k a month +18.16%, units triple +15.60%, ASP held +13.70%, HSBC 1.6T mix +36.45% (all carded). No public optical consensus found.

Bounds: the FY26 10-K says the AEC ramp 'contributed over 99% of the increase in revenue' ($898.3M) [src 12; the phrase is in the 10-K's MD&A, located by EDGAR full-text search, src 51], so non-AEC revenue rose at most ~$9M in FY26; the FY25 10-K says AECs were over 95% of the $267.1M product-sales increase and FY24 product sales were $145.0M, with product engineering services $12.1M and IP license $12.5M in FY25 [src 30]. inputs_detail.source: FY2026 10-K end-customer table: Customer D 33%, Customer B 32%, Customer E 19% (direct-billing basis Customer A 49%) [src 12]. Q1 FY27 10-Q end-customer table: D 33%, C 28%, E 13%, F 10% (direct basis A 43%, 57% of receivables) [src 11]; CFO: 'our largest customer was a third of our revenue at 33%' [src 22].
inputs_detail.derivation: Base 0.33 (FY26) and held at 0.33 in FY27-29 (Q1 FY27 33%; management expects 3-4 customers above 10% [src 22], i.e. diversification comes through the other customers, which the shares carry). Formula: each segment's revenue = TAM x share x 1000 x (1 - 0.33) / (1 - top_customer_pct). At the base path the factor is 1. Moving the driver to T means the top customer buys less (or more) while every other customer stays as the TAM x share build says: total revenue scales by 0.67 / (1 - T) and the top customer's revenue by T x 0.67 / (0.33 x (1 - T)). Bear: T 0.33 -> 0.21 cuts total revenue 15.2% and the top customer's revenue 46% (a 1.6T AEC dual-source to Marvell at 15-20% lower prices, agents 1-5). The top customer's product mix is not disclosed; the term applies to copper and optical alike (the CFO says these hyperscalers buy more than AECs [src 22]). Variant view: on the direct-billing basis (43%) the same customer-loss story is larger; the end-customer basis is used because the sourcing decision is the end customer's. QUARTERS (2026-10-29): 0.33 every quarter: FY26 10-K end-customer D 33% (the FY figure is used for each FY26 quarter: an annual concentration figure applied to each base quarter, so the base quarters aggregate to the 10-K's 0.33; the 10-Q end-customer tables give the quarter's largest end customer at 35% Q1 (acc 0001807794-25-000021), 42% Q2 (0001628280-25-054549), 39% Q3 (0001628280-26-014017), Q4 not disclosed, with the letters rotating between filings, so the quarter tops are not the FY top); Q1 FY27 10-Q D 33% [src 11]; held forward. The term is 1 at 0.33, so it moves revenue only in scenarios.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: gm_optical = non-GAAP gross margin on optical revenue; Credo discloses no line margin. Booked since your 2026-11-16 17:36Z pick: the Coherent anchor from Q2 FY27 (optical 59.2% revenue-weighted, Q2-Q4 FY27 62.3% / 59.7% / 57.4%, then 56.8% / 57.1% FY28-29). Peer build: ZF optics = a module maker's gross margin A + the chip margin Credo keeps on the DSP and PIC it makes itself, 0.65 x s x (1 - A), with s the DSP+PIC share of module cost; merchant DSPs and PICs stay at 65%. s = 36% (DSP 25%, midpoint of 20-30%, src 79, 80; PIC 11%, midpoint of 8-14%, an estimate: no source gives a PIC share, src 80). The estimated range 28-44% gives ZF 57.1-62.5% on a 47.5% anchor. To reach 65% on ZF the anchor would have to be 54.3%, above every module margin in the evidence. Anchors, each checked for like-for-like: Coherent 40.6% non-GAAP Q1 FY27 (src 78): scaled and non-China, but it makes its own lasers (src 80), so laser margin a laser-buying ZF maker does not earn is in it; 17.7% Industrial revenue; margin rising (38.7% a year earlier) in a supply-short market. ZF 54.5%: the booked anchor (it moved the target -4.68% from the 65% booking, to $195.15 on that set). Deep Fundamental's 'SiPh module gross margins are currently 30-40%' (src 79, Tegus experts): same product type, dated September 2024, before the 2025-26 tightness. 35% gives ZF 50.2%, -2.34% ($206.98) against the booked set. ZF 45.9%, -4.70% ($201.98). Singularity's 15-30% for scaled module makers (src 80, analyst estimate; includes contract manufacturers with thinner reported margins): a floor. 22.5% gives ZF 40.6%, -7.56% ($195.91). InnoLight 46.59% / Eoptolink 48.46% H1 2026 (src 77; that page failed to load on 2026-11-17, the same figures are on remio, src 95, and InnoLight's on 36Kr, src 96) are the closest business model (they buy lasers and DSPs, src 80), but both are China-domiciled. So they are replaced as the central anchor and sized for reference only: +2.88% from Q2 FY27, +2.91% from FY28 against the booked anchor.
